extracted.intended_audience: generic drug applicants (ANDA filers), generic drug manufacturers, ANDA legal/regulatory counsel, brand sponsors and patent holders
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on Paragraph IV patent certifications, FDA's Paragraph IV Certification List, 180-day exclusivity considerations, and suitability petition requirements for ANDA submissions. Intended to inform generic applicants and stakeholders about procedural and substantive standards governing challenges to Orange Book patents and permitted RLD differences via suitability petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph IV certification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A generic applicant must provide in its ANDA a certification that, to the best of its knowledge, a patent submitted to FDA by the brand sponsor and listed in the Orange Book is invalid, unenforceable, or will not be infringed by the generic product (a 'paragraph IV certification').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certification must be contained in a substantially complete ANDA. The first applicant(s) submitting a substantially complete ANDA with a paragraph IV certification to at least one Orange Book patent are generally eligible for 180-day exclusivity. The page explains the legal basis (Hatch-Waxman) and links to additional FDA guidance (e.g., 180-Day Exclusivity Q&A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirement to initiate patent challenge
rubrics_metrics.description: The generic applicant that submits a paragraph IV certification must notify the brand product sponsor and any patent holder of the submission of the ANDA and the patent challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notice is a prerequisite to patent litigation that can trigger statutory stays and exclusivity consequences. The page explains the downstream effects (see 45-day window and 30-month stay).

rubrics_metrics.name: 45-day window for infringement suit and 30-month stay
rubrics_metrics.description: If the brand sponsor or patent holder files an infringement suit against the generic applicant within 45 days of the ANDA notification, FDA approval to market the generic drug is generally postponed for 30 months unless the patent expires or is adjudged invalid or not infringed sooner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 30-month stay period provides time for the brand/patent holder to assert patent rights in court before generic approval. The guidance clarifies the typical effect on approval timing and exclusivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-to-file (first applicant) eligibility for 180-day exclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: The first company or companies to submit a substantially complete ANDA that contains a paragraph IV certification to at least one Orange Book patent are generally eligible for 180 days of market exclusivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is subject to statutory and regulatory provisions (including post-MMA rules) and to forfeiture provisions. FDA provides additional clarifications (e.g., draft guidance on 180-day exclusivity). The page notes complexities (multiple first applicants, adjustments for refusal-to-receive reconsideration, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph IV Certification List — Active Ingredient Name
rubrics_metrics.description: The list will include the established (nonproprietary) name of the active ingredient(s) in the drug product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a reporting column on the PIV Certification List to help identify the drug product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph IV Certification List — Dosage Form
rubrics_metrics.description: The list will include the dosage form of the drug product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as part of the PIV Certification List columns (e.g., tablet, solution, intrathecal solution) to aid applicants in identifying relevant listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph IV Certification List — Strength
rubrics_metrics.description: The list will include the strength(s) of the drug product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths are listed in the PIV Certification List so applicants can see which strengths had paragraph IV submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph IV Certification List — RLD name and NDA number
rubrics_metrics.description: The list will show the proprietary name (if any) of the Reference Listed Drug (RLD) and its NDA number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This column helps link the paragraph IV submissions to the corresponding RLD/NDA in the Orange Book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph IV Certification List — Date of First PIV Submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The list will reflect the first date that a substantially complete application containing a paragraph IV certification to at least one Orange Book patent was submitted (this may be an original ANDA, an amendment, or a supplement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries may be blank retrospectively if FDA has not updated older records. Some drug products will show 'pre-MMA' instead of a date where pre-MMA statutory provisions apply; see pre-MMA guidance for complexities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of 'pre-MMA' entries for Date of First PIV Submission
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Pre-MMA' entries indicate submissions subject to the FD&C Act provisions in effect prior to the Medicare Prescription Drug, Improvement, and Modernization Act of 2003, where patent-by-patent analysis makes listing individual dates impractical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult FDA's 180-Day Exclusivity Q&A for more information about pre-MMA applicability and complexities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph IV Certification List — Number of potential first applicant ANDAs submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: This column indicates the number of substantially complete ANDAs that contained a paragraph IV certification to at least one RLD patent on the first date such a certification was submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA may adjust this number over time (e.g., if it grants reconsideration of a refusal to receive an ANDA). This helps identify how many potential first applicants filed on the first day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph IV Certification List — 180-Day Decision Status (definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: This column indicates whether FDA has made (or deferred) a decision regarding eligibility for 180-day exclusivity: 'eligible' (approved and considered eligible at approval), 'deferred' (approved but no determination), 'non-forfeiture' (tentative approval of a subsequent applicant based on a first applicant's eligibility), or 'extinguished' (180-day exclusivity extinguished because all first applicants forfeited or relinquished eligibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The column is cumulative with the most recent decision first. FDA may later change a decision if new events occur (e.g., subsequent forfeiture after an earlier non-forfeiture decision). Many decisions requiring analysis are made in the context of specific ANDAs that are otherwise eligible for approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph IV Certification List — 180-Day Decision Posting Date
rubrics_metrics.description: This column reflects the month and year that FDA updated the PIV Certification List to reflect the corresponding 180-day decision status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This column is cumulative with the most recent decision date first and helps track when FDA posted its determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph IV Certification List — Date of First Approval of 'First Applicant' ANDA
rubrics_metrics.description: This column indicates the first date on which a first applicant's ANDA received final approval; if multiple first applicants, only the first approval date is posted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to document when the first applicant actually obtained approval (relevant to exclusivity timing). Approval letters are posted on the Drugs@FDA website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph IV Certification List — Date of First Commercial Marketing
rubrics_metrics.description: This column reflects the date of first commercial marketing by any first applicant and, along with the Date of First Approval, shows the time between approval and commercial launch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a first applicant begins commercial marketing and is eligible for 180-day exclusivity, the Orange Book posts a Patent Challenge (PC) code on the approved ANDA(s) to indicate the start and expiration of the 180-day exclusivity period. If FDA deferred the exclusivity determination at approval, a PC code will not be entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph IV Certification List — Expiration Date of Last Qualifying Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: This column lists the last expiration date of any patent(s) that qualify any first applicant for 180-day exclusivity for a given drug product; it indicates when 180-day exclusivity will no longer be available due to patent expiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple applications were submitted on the first day, patents with at least one PIV certification among the submissions are considered; patents only covered by PIII certifications are not considered. This column does not reflect pediatric exclusivity associated with the last qualifying patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability petition permissible differences
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may submit a suitability petition under 505(j)(2)(C) and 21 CFR 314.93 requesting permission to submit an ANDA for a generic product that differs from the RLD in route of administration, dosage form, strength, or has one different active ingredient in a fixed-combination product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ANDA citing an unapproved suitability petition will not be received because it lacks a legal basis. The grounds for FDA approval of such petitions are set out in 21 CFR 314.93(e). The determination that an ANDA will be approved is made only during the ANDA review; petition approval alone does not guarantee ANDA approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessing and tracking suitability petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of submitted suitability petitions and FDA responses are viewable on regulations.gov (searchable by docket number or drug product name), and comments to pending petitions may be submitted there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OGD previously posted suitability tracking reports but recommends searching regulations.gov for the most up-to-date information; two historical PDF tracking reports (updated Aug 2015) are linked for reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture provisions and timing for 180-day exclusivity decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain statutory forfeiture provisions (e.g., failure-to-obtain-test-approval within 30 months, failure-to-market, withdrawal-of-application, amendment-of-certification, expiration-of-all-patents) can extinguish or forfeit 180-day exclusivity eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions under these provisions are generally made once facts are settled and often in the context of specific ANDAs otherwise eligible for approval. Many factors (patent expiry, withdrawals, timing of approvals) can influence eligibility up to the time an application is ready for approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDA's authoritative-source caveat and data-driven decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA aims to provide accurate information in the PIV Certification List but will make regulatory decisions based on data and information in relevant applications, not the list itself; entries may not be updated while FDA is evaluating issues impacting a drug product's listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders should discuss discrepancies with FDA's Patent and Exclusivity Team (PET) via the provided email. The page cautions that the list is for informational purposes and not a substitute for data in applications.
